flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
I've had so many. I feel like kids have hard times regulating their emotions, especially the younger ones who can't speak yet. So I'll use biting, for example, like I'll have a kid who is playing with the toy and then another kid wants that toy. So then it starts to kind of be like a back and forth and then they'll kind of result into biting. And I kind of understand that's just their way of communicating like they don't like whatever is going on back to like, you know, the toy situation. So they don't like that a friend is trying to take the toy or a friend has a toy that they want. So they go into that. So I kind of just let them know like, you know, teeth are not for biting and kind of just try and redirect them. Most of the time we have multiple toys that are the same exact toy that they're fighting over. It may just be a little different. So if I can make that toy and turn it into something so much more fun for them. Like, oh, my gosh, look at this. We have this. And, you know, just kind of like give them that redirection is kind of how I like to go about that. Or I have kids who throw toys, let them know like, hey, like this is not for throwing. If you want to throw something, I can, you know, a plush ball or a beanbag, something soft. I'll throw it. We can catch it back and forth, kind of do that. Just I just like to redirect them instead of, you know, resulting. Into anger and dying.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed at work with children present. What did you do to manage yourself?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q4 Attempt 1]
Um, so at my current school, I love how you mentioned your ratios. At my current school, I am sometimes alone with kids of just me and I'll have like 17 kids by myself. They're different ages. I'll have twos, threes, and then it'll jump to five and then I'll have a six year old or two. So with that, I kind of, I've never tried to show my emotions in front of kids. I feel like kids can read you from a mile away. They can feel every emotion. If you're upset, they feel upset. If you're sad, you know, they can see that. So I never want to show that in front of my kids. So I just would ask my director if I can have a break, you know, get some help. I like to communicate. With my director or because like I said, in the afternoons, I'm by myself. So I don't have another employee to communicate with. But my director, I do kind of communicate with her like, you know, if I can just have some help, or can I take a break? Just that type of things just like step away, regroup, and then just come back and be my happy self. But yeah, like I said, I don't like to show any type of sad emotion or upset. Or overstimulated in front of the kids. They will pick up on that and it'll show. Listen to music. I like to listen to jazz, gospel music, drink some water. Sometimes I just need a snack, you know, just like a little sweet treat. I have a little snack in my purse. Yeah, I'm just sitting quiet, you know, with my kids. Like I said, it's me and 17 of them. So sometimes, yeah. So sometimes I just need that moment to myself to just sit in quiet. I don't even want to go on my phone. I'm just eating a cracker, drinking some water, and I'm just sitting.
